string-array.name: driving_tips
string-array.item: Open the throttle progressively and hold it; avoid repeated press-and-release — it suited lead-acid, not lithium.
A steady moderate speed is most efficient: consumption, current and heat rise fast with speed.
Start gently: the highest current happens when accelerating from a stop, and that is what strains the weakest cell.
Don’t run the battery flat; head back with at least 20 % left.
In the cold less capacity is available; expect less range and ride gently until the battery warms up.
Watch “Cells over time”: if one cell keeps sagging under load, ease acceleration and check the balance.

resources.string: What you pay for 1 kWh of electricity, as on your electricity bill (e.g. 0.80 or 1.20).\nGT-BMS multiplies it by the energy that went into the battery, plus about 15 % lost in the charger, to give the cost of each charge, trip and kilometre.\nLeave it at 0 to hide costs.
Short name or symbol shown next to costs: MAD, DH, €, \$, DZD, TND…\nIt is only a label; nothing is converted.
Optional. Price of one litre of petrol in the same currency.\nWith the fuel use below, each trip also shows what the same distance would have cost with a petrol vehicle.

Optional. How many litres a comparable petrol vehicle burns per 100 km (a petrol moped: about 2–3; a small car: 5–7).\nExample: 2.5 L/100 km at 17 per litre → 10 km cost 4.25 in fuel.\nLeave empty to hide the comparison.
